chapters.title: The burnt offering
chapters.summary: From the tabernacle God explains the burnt offering, wholly burned on the altar as a pleasing aroma and an act of complete devotion. Offerings could be cattle, sheep, goats or birds.

chapters.title: The grain offering
chapters.summary: Instructions for offerings of flour, oil and incense, given in thanks. Part is burned and the rest goes to the priests. Every offering is to be seasoned with salt.

chapters.title: The peace offering
chapters.summary: The fellowship or peace offering celebrates being at peace with God. The fat belongs to the Lord, and eating fat or blood is forbidden.

chapters.title: The sin offering
chapters.summary: For sins committed unintentionally, by a priest, the whole community, a leader or an ordinary person, a sin offering is made so that they may be forgiven.

chapters.title: The guilt offering
chapters.summary: Offerings for specific failings, such as keeping silent as a witness or touching something unclean, with provision for the poor to bring birds or flour instead.

chapters.title: Repayment and the altar fire
chapters.summary: Someone who cheats a neighbor must repay in full plus a fifth before bringing a guilt offering. The priests must keep the fire on the altar burning continually.

chapters.title: The priests' portions
chapters.summary: More detail on the guilt and peace offerings and which parts belong to the priests. Fat and blood must never be eaten.

chapters.title: Aaron and his sons ordained
chapters.summary: Moses washes, robes and anoints Aaron and his sons before the whole assembly, and they remain at the tent of meeting for seven days.

chapters.title: The priests begin
chapters.summary: Aaron offers the first sacrifices for himself and the people and blesses them. The glory of the Lord appears, and fire from the Lord consumes the offering.

chapters.title: Nadab and Abihu
chapters.summary: Aaron's sons offer unauthorized fire before the Lord and are struck down. The priests are told to distinguish between holy and common, clean and unclean.

chapters.title: Clean and unclean animals
chapters.summary: Rules about which land animals, fish, birds and insects may be eaten. The reason given is holiness: be holy, for I am holy.

chapters.title: After childbirth
chapters.summary: A mother's purification after giving birth, completed with an offering, with a pair of birds allowed for families who cannot afford a lamb.

chapters.title: Skin diseases
chapters.summary: The priest examines skin diseases and mildew on clothing. Those with an infectious disease must live outside the camp until they are clean.

chapters.title: Cleansing and restoration
chapters.summary: The ritual for restoring someone healed of a skin disease to the community, and for cleansing a house affected by mildew.

chapters.title: Bodily discharges
chapters.summary: Laws about uncleanness from bodily discharges for men and women, and how to become clean again, so that Israel would not defile God's dwelling among them.

chapters.title: The Day of Atonement
chapters.summary: Once a year the high priest enters the Most Holy Place to make atonement for himself and the people. One goat is sacrificed and the scapegoat carries the people's sins into the wilderness.

chapters.title: The life is in the blood
chapters.summary: Sacrifices must be brought to the tabernacle, not offered elsewhere. Eating blood is forbidden, because the life of a creature is in the blood, given for atonement.

chapters.title: Unlawful relations
chapters.summary: Israel must not follow the practices of Egypt or Canaan. Forbidden sexual relationships are listed, along with child sacrifice to Molech.

chapters.title: Love your neighbor
chapters.summary: A wide range of laws on holiness in everyday life: honoring parents, leaving gleanings for the poor, honest dealing, and loving your neighbor and the stranger as yourself.

chapters.title: Penalties for sin
chapters.summary: The penalties for child sacrifice, consulting mediums, cursing parents and sexual sins, because Israel is set apart to belong to God.

chapters.title: Holiness of the priests
chapters.summary: Special standards for the priests in mourning, marriage and physical fitness for service at the altar, because they offer the food of their God.

chapters.title: Eating the holy offerings
chapters.summary: Who may eat the holy offerings, and the requirement that sacrificed animals be without defect.

chapters.title: The appointed feasts
chapters.summary: The Sabbath and Israel's yearly feasts: Passover, Unleavened Bread, Firstfruits, Weeks, Trumpets, the Day of Atonement and Tabernacles.

chapters.title: Lamp, bread and blasphemy
chapters.summary: Pure oil for the lamp and twelve loaves set before the Lord each Sabbath. A man who blasphemes the Name is judged, and the same law applies to stranger and native.

chapters.title: Sabbath year and Jubilee
chapters.summary: Every seventh year the land rests. Every fiftieth year is a Jubilee: land returns to its families and Israelite servants go free, for the land belongs to God.

chapters.title: Blessings and warnings
chapters.summary: God promises rain, peace and His presence if Israel obeys, and warns of growing judgment if they reject Him. Even then He will remember His covenant.

chapters.title: Vows and dedications
chapters.summary: How to value and redeem people, animals, houses and fields dedicated to the Lord, and the tithe that belongs to Him.
